Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

quorum (development version)

  • The package has a logo.
  • README lists related packages.
  • CI runs lintr (report-only) and test coverage.
  • CITATION.cff states the package’s current version.

quorum 0.1.0

  • Renamed from flexyBayesOrchestra and re-dedicated as the orchestra’s consensus layer (plan approved 2026-09-02). quorum compares lenses and never fits a model of its own: every lens is a member’s fitter behind an adapter with declared independence, expressiveness and scope. A quorum of independent lenses must agree before an answer is carried; no quorum means abstain. The previous capabilities stay as the on-ramps by which non-hub estimates become lenses (ensemble ingestion, surrogates, the koine backend); their function names are unchanged.
  • New: quorum_abstention() / is_quorum_abstention(), the package’s typed decline (classed quorum_abstention / orchestra_refusal).
  • Imports: gains orchestraManifest and S7.
  • The flexyBayesOrchestra_abstention class stamp is now quorum_abstention; the flexyBayesOrchestra.koine_activated option is now quorum.koine_activated.
  • The lens contract and registry (lens(), lens_from_draws(), lens_from_fit(), lens_koine(), lens_status_quo(), lens_mechanism(), and the roster register_lens()/get_lens()/list_lenses()/ clear_lenses()) declare a member’s estimate as a quorum_lens, with its shared components, its expressible response shapes and its scope, so any producer can register an adapter without a code change here.
  • The TMB lens (lens_tmb()) fits glmmTMB’s Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood and samples the very TMB objective that fit produced with tmbstan’s NUTS sampler, contributing a second Laplace implementation and one objective sampled two ways, with the hub’s default priors matched as far as glmmTMB’s syntax allows and declared when they are not.
  • The independence ledger (quorum_independence()) counts what every pair of lenses shares across sampler, objective, priors and data preparation and converts the count into the evidential weight a quorum reads before treating agreement as corroboration.
  • The agreement layer (agreement_thresholds(), agreement_pairwise(), agreement_status(), agreement_matrix()) re-derives the hub’s triangulate() comparison semantics over lens draws component by component, proven bit-identical to the hub’s own output on the same draws.
  • Policy and resolution (quorum_policy(), policy_committed(), lens_contribution(), quorum_resolve(), quorum_compare_policies()) generalise Study A0’s hand-written two-lens cascade into a declared fallback order over any number of lenses, with the two committed conventions the cascade replaced kept as priceable policy objects.
  • The front door (quorum()) gates each lens on its own scope, asks it to fit, compares what came back, weighs the comparison by declared independence, and resolves it through the policy into a quorum_verdict: concordant, discordant, no_quorum (abstain) or not_computed.
  • The manifest (quorum_manifest()) emits a verdict as an orchestra_manifest with inferential_target = "consensus", stamped grounded only when a contributing lens is grounded and the lenses did not read the same upstream data fact.
  • The Study A0 cascade is reproduced bit-identically from the package on the shipped fixture: 200 decision cells resolve to the recorded tiers and rates, mechanism carrying 150, statistical 48 and the status quo 2.

The quorum -> decideR seam

  • A concordant verdict now carries the carried lens’s posterior into its manifest, in outputs, hashed with the contributions table and the summary. Before this the lenses’ draws were discarded once agreement had been computed, so a consensus manifest left the package with nothing a decision layer could read: decideR::decide_from_manifest() found no draws and failed on the shape. The seam between the orchestra’s consensus layer and its decision layer was open, on the exact target the consensus layer exists to produce.

  • A verdict that issued no number carries no draws. Only a concordant status over a single resolved cell releases the posterior. A no_quorum, discordant or not_computed verdict emits outputs = NULL, so nothing downstream can price a number the quorum declined to issue.

  • The draws are read through the lens object’s own property rather than coerced. quorum_draws holds a named list of numeric vectors for the parameters kind, and coercing the object directly would have produced a one-column list-matrix without failing, which is the quiet kind of wrong.

Documentation

  • Help pages no longer point to the triangulate() functions removed from flexyBayes in 0.14.0; emit_koine() now names lens_from_fit() and agreement_pairwise() as the way to compare a koine fit with another fit.

Carried from flexyBayesOrchestra

  • Relicensed from GPL (>= 3) to MIT (orchestra-wide licence unification, 2026-09-02). No code change.

  • emit_koine()’s abstained exit now stamps the outer wrapper as a dispatchable orchestra decline. The returned flexybayes_koine object already carried a real, correctly-typed nested koine_abstention at $koine whenever koine’s corner or convergence gate declined a model, but the OUTER object – what a caller (and the orchestra’s refusal-contract gate, is_orchestra_decline()) actually holds – was always plain c("flexybayes_koine", "list"), invisible to any predicate keyed on a _refusal / _abstention class suffix or the orchestra_refusal marker. The abstained exit now prepends c("quorum_abstention", "orchestra_refusal") to that class vector; a contributed fit is unchanged. Existing consumers are unaffected: inherits(x, "flexybayes_koine"), is.list(x), and every *.flexybayes_koine S3 method still dispatch, since S3 method lookup scans the whole class vector and "flexybayes_koine" is still present, just no longer first. WHAT is refused is unchanged – only HOW the abstained case is signalled to a class-based predicate.

  • emit_koine() now fits a multi-environment trial instead of abstaining on every one (FBO-06). The capability gate refused any model with more than one random term, which matched the single group argument the companion drove – so koine’s fourth column was empty on exactly the crossed (1 | variety) + (1 | trial) structure the study series’ statistical lens is built from. koine 0.3.0 fields that structure through the groups argument of koine_pass_from_design() (read from the installed namespace, not assumed), and the MET case is now routed there: the gate admits two plain random intercepts, the group SDs koine reports as tau_<grouping> canonicalise to sd_<grouping>, and extras$model_info records the resolved re_structure. Below koine 0.3.0 a two-grouping model returns a typed abstention naming the version floor, and more than two groupings (or any non-intercept random term) still abstains before any koine call. Suggests: raised to koine (>= 0.3.0); the slot-activation floor stays at 0.2.0, which is still the floor for the single-intercept corner.

  • The kernR cme conformer no longer extrapolates confidently (FBO-01). The conditional-mean smoother’s weights decay to zero as a prediction point leaves the design, which drove the mean to zero and the reported sigma^2 (1 + ||w||^2) sd down to its in-design floor – on the reference design the conformer returned y_mean = 0.000000, y_sd = 0.298104 at (a, b) = (12, 12) against a true 71.463427, the same sd it reports in the middle of the design. The conformer now records the smoother’s weight mass across the training design at fit time and raises a classed fb_surrogate_cme_abstention condition (the _abstention suffix the constellation’s shared decline predicate keys on) wherever the mass falls below weight_mass_frac (default 0.5) times the least-supported design point’s mass, naming the reference rff surrogate as the extrapolation fallback. The floor is tunable at fit time (weight_mass_frac, weight_mass_floor) and per call (weight_mass_floor), and setting it to 0 restores the ungated behaviour deliberately.

  • %||% defined locally (FBO-03). The infix was used nine times across R/ but defined nowhere in the package and imported from nowhere, so it resolved only via base::%||% – absent below R 4.4.0, against a declared floor of R (>= 4.1.0). Added a package-local %||% in R/utils.R.

  • Aggregated multi-kernel MMD PPC re-calibrated (FBO-07). .mmd_agg()’s per-permutation p-values (pj) ranked each permutation replicate against its own bandwidth’s null including itself, while the observed statistic’s p-value (p_obs) was ranked against the same null excluding it – an asymmetric comparison that miscalibrates the aggregated test’s level. Both are now ranked against the pooled set of the observed statistic and its B permutation replicates together, per bandwidth.

  • Contract ownership corrected in the shipped documentation (FBO-04). inst/surrogate_contract.md, inst/ensemble_source_contract.md, both vignettes, and the roxygen for fit_surrogate(), predict.fb_surrogate(), register_surrogate(), fb_ensemble(), as_fb_ensemble(), register_ensemble_source(), and fb_pesto() attributed contracts C5 (fb_ensemble) and C7 (fb_surrogate) to flexyBayes; flexyBayes 0.9.2 exports neither verb. Ownership is now attributed to quorum throughout, which is where both contracts are actually implemented; a reader following the shipped contract no longer calls a function that does not exist.

  • getting-started vignette replaced (FBO-08). The shipped vignette was a self-declared build-clean stub (library() and nothing else). It now walks the three composition seams (ingest an ensemble, emulate it, triangulate with koine), including the governing predictive-distribution equation for the reference rff surrogate with its citation.

  • surrogate-workflow vignette gains three captioned, interpreted figures (FBO-09). A predictive band against truth across and beyond the design (the picture that would have shown an emulator reporting in-design-sized uncertainty off-design), the dense cross-output covariance beside its rank-1 reconstruction, and the ES-MDA inversion misfit trace. Grammar and false-attribution issues in its prose fixed alongside.

  • Governing mathematics added to predict.fb_surrogate() (FBO-15). The reference surrogate’s predictive mean/variance, previously stated only in # comments, is now a \deqn block with a citation (Bishop, 2006). @examples added to predict.fb_surrogate(), fb_surrogate_ppc(), and as_fb_ensemble() – the three headline consumers that previously shipped with none.

  • koine_status() documentation corrected (FBO-12). Its @description still read “provisioned but dormant until koine ships a programmatic, re-entrant model builder”; the slot has been active by default since 2026-06-08. Rewritten to describe the activated state.

  • README refreshed (FBO-16). Dropped the stale “dormant koine slot” and unimplemented “gretaR engine, registered against the backend registry” bullets (this package registers no gretaR anything); added a minimal runnable ingest-emulate-predict example.

  • Non-ASCII arrow in as_fb_ensemble() roxygen replaced with -> (FBO-19; tools::checkRd() flagged it as non-ASCII content without a declared encoding).

  • quorum_resolve() treats both "ungrounded" (orchestraManifest 0.2.0) and the older "[unverified]" as an ungrounded input.

quorum 0.0.0.9000

  • koine genomic fourth opinion (koine_genomic_lens()). The koine fourth opinion, specialised for genomics: it runs the established REML genomic BLUP (via ) on the same data and emits a genomic lens that flexyBayes::triangulate_genomic() (>= 0.8.0) consumes as a fourth column. In genomics the orchestra’s value is not replacing the decades of established REML / field-standard tools but catching divergence – “our Bayesian GEBVs disagree with sommer’s REML – investigate.” The lens contract keeps flexyBayes core lean: core never depends on the field tools; the companion produces the lens and core compares it. sommer is a Suggests-only oracle (never on a fit path). GEMMA / rrBLUP (GWAS) and BGLR (Bayesian marker) lenses are the same pattern, planned.
  • koine fourth-opinion backend activated (2026-06-08). emit_koine() ports koine’s real opinion synthesis (koine::koine_pass_from_design() -> koine::synthesise() -> koine::koine_opinion_draws()) and returns a self-naming flexybayes_koine fit. S3 methods registered on flexyBayes core’s exported fb_as_draws_simple() and canonical_names() generics let core’s generic triangulate() consume the koine fit as its fourth column with no flexyBayes core edit (the lean-0.7.0 boundary holds). koine fields a population GLM + a single random intercept (1 | g) for gaussian / binomial / poisson; it abstains outside its corner. The slot (koine_status()) is now live: activation floor koine (>= 0.2.0), gated by options(quorum.koine_activated = TRUE) (the default). koine moved to Suggests; posterior added to Suggests.
  • Initial development version. quorum is the orchestra-composition companion to flexyBayes, created by the flexyBayes lean-core split: it carries the surrogate emulators (fit_surrogate(), fb_surrogate_ies(), fb_surrogate_ppc()), ensemble sources (fb_ensemble(), as_fb_ensemble(), read_fb_ensemble(), verify_fb_ensemble(), register_ensemble_source()), the PESTO ensemble-derived priors (fb_pesto(), fb_prior_from_ensemble()), and the dormant koine fourth-opinion slot (koine_status()) that previously lived in flexyBayes core.
  • .onLoad() registers the PESTO / kernR surrogate conformers when those member packages are installed, so fit_surrogate(method = "gp" / "cme") is discoverable – restoring the behaviour that lived in flexyBayes before the split.
